Write instructions for playing the flute.

1. Start by assembling your flute. Make sure all of the parts are properly aligned, and slide the head joint into the body. Twist the joint slightly to ensure a tight fit, but be gentle to avoid damage.

2. Before you begin playing, you will need to create a sound by blowing into the flute. Position your mouth on the mouthpiece, with your lower lip directly below the embouchure hole. Blow gently into the hole, angling your breath slightly downwards.

3. Once you have created a sound, practice holding long, sustained notes. This will help you focus on your breath control and tone quality.

4. Next, learn how to play different notes by using your fingers to cover and uncover the holes on the instrument. Start with the lowest note (C) by covering all of the holes, and then gradually work your way up the scale by uncovering the holes one at a time.

5. Practice finger exercises and scales to improve your technique and intonation. There are many resources available online or in instructional books that can help guide your practice.

6. Experiment with different articulations and dynamics to add variation and expression to your playing. Try playing legato (smooth and connected) and staccato (short and detached) notes, and experiment with playing louder and softer.

7. Remember to take breaks as needed and stretch your hand and arm muscles regularly, especially if you are playing for an extended period of time. Practice regularly to build endurance and improve your skills over time.

"Using matrix factorization algorithms, design and implement a recommendation engine that utilizes user interactions and feedback to suggest personalized products or services based on their preferences and history."

I can provide a high-level overview of how a recommendation engine utilizing matrix factorization algorithms can be designed and implemented. 

matrix factorization algorithms are widely used in recommendation systems to uncover hidden patterns and relationships among users and items based on their past interactions. The goal is to learn a model that can predict the likelihood of a user liking or consuming an item that they have not yet interacted with.

here are the major steps involved in designing and implementing a recommendation engine using matrix factorization:

1. Data collection: collect data on user interactions with products or services. This can include data such as user ratings, purchase histories, search histories, and social media behavior.

2. Data preparation: clean and preprocess the data to remove noise, handle missing values, and transform the data into a suitable format for matrix factorization.

3. Matrix factorization: apply a matrix factorization technique such as singular value decomposition (svd) or alternating least squares (als) to factorize the user-item interaction matrix into two lower rank matrices representing user and item latent factors.

4. Model training: train the model using the factorized matrices to estimate the latent factors of users and items.

5. Prediction generation: generate personalized recommendations for each user by predicting the likelihood of a user consuming an item based on their latent factors and the item's latent factors.

6. Evaluation: evaluate the performance of the recommendation engine using metrics such as precision, recall, and mean average precision (map) to measure the accuracy and relevancy of the recommendations.

7. Deployment: deploy the recommendation engine as an api, web service, or mobile app that can serve personalized recommendations in real-time based on user input.

overall, building a recommendation engine using matrix factorization requires expertise in machine learning, data engineering, and software development. It also requires a large amount of high-quality data to train the model and generate accurate recommendations.

It can be used to convey themes and ideas that are difficult to express in literal language. Metaphor is a type of symbolism that involves comparing two seemingly unrelated things to create a deeper understanding of a concept or idea.

authors can use symbolism and metaphor in many ways to convey deeper meanings about characters and themes. They can create symbolic characters or objects that represent a larger idea or theme in the story. For example, a white dove may symbolize peace or freedom. They can also use metaphors to create comparisons that highlight the similarities and differences between two concepts. symbolism and metaphor can also be used to create ambiguity and mystery in a story. By using symbolic language, authors leave it up to the reader to interpret its meaning, leading to multiple interpretations and even debate.

overall, symbolism and metaphor are powerful literary devices that can enrich a story's meaning and themes beyond the literal language. By using these devices, authors can convey deeper meanings about their characters and themes, creating a more engaging and thought-provoking reading experience.

Sometimes dreams come true and miracles happen and high protein chocolate chip cookies come into existence.
When you want something sweet, it’s hard to resist the classic chocolate chip cookie. It’s sweet. It’s comforting. It’s loyal. It’s basically your BFF.
But, for those times you don’t want your BFF to be loaded with refined sugar, simple carbs, and unhealthy fats, you’re in luck because I gave your BFF a make-over! It’s pretty much the chocolate chip cookie of your dreams. These deep dish cookies are full of protein, low in fat, grain free, and low in sugar. No joke! A typical chocolate chip cookie has about 13 grams of sugar and 2 grams of protein. Howevah, these delicious treats have a whopping 8 grams of protein and a measly 2 grams of refined sugar!
And because I am with everything else in life, I am also indecisive about wanting a super chewy cookie or a really crispy one. So, if you needed another reason to love these deep dish cookies, you get the best of both worlds with them! They have a nice, crispy edge with a soft, chewy center. The trick to getting this combo is baking them in a muffin tin. Not only is it easy and convenient, but it also keeps the cookies from spreading out while baking, giving them the chewy center. And because the batter is touching the pan all the way around, you get a nice, crispy edge. It’s like the corner piece of a pan of brownies, but all around! Once again, it’s like unicorns invaded your dreams and made your wishes come true.
And whipping up these high protein treats couldn’t be any easier. As long as you’ve got a blender or food processor you’re in business, because we’re going to puree some chickpeas. Just trust me on this one. These little gems are going to give your cookies some texture, chewiness, and replaces the flour so the cookies are grain-free. Once you’ve got them pureed, all you need to do is mix the dry ingredients, stir together the wet ingredients, and then combine that all together.
Preheat the oven to 325 F. Grease a 12 cup muffin tin.
In a food processor or blender, puree the chickpeas with the water until smooth.
In a large bowl, add the coconut flour, protein powder, sweetener, baking powder and soda, and salt.
In a seperate bowl, combine the chickpea puree, egg, yogurt, milk, oil, and vanilla. Stir or whisk until fully combined.
Add the wet ingredients to the dry and stir until fully incorporated.
Evenly distribute the batter into the prepared muffin tins. It will be about 1.5 - 2 Tbsps of dough per cookie.
Smooth out the batter so batter touches the edges of the pan, but don't press/flatten the dough.
Bake for 14 min. Or until the edges of the cookies turn golden brown and a toothpick inserted into the center of the cookie dough comes out clean.
Allow the cookies to cool completely in the pan.
Feel free to top with nut butter, jam, or more chocolate and eat 'em up!

What are some must-visit destinations in Washington, D.C. According to the fashion girl’s guide? Answer according to: The Fashion Girl’s Guide To Washington, D.C.
Many will flock to the nation’s capital next weekend for the presidential inauguration and the Women’s March on Washington, which is set to take place the day after the official festivities. It’s been a while since we’ve thought about D.C. In terms of must-visit destinations—it’s so difficult to focus on any one city, with all of these places to see—but it’s absolutely a place worth adding to your bucket list for 2017. Here, our guide on where to stay, what to eat and how to shop (and more!) when you’re in the nation’s capital.
If you're going to D.C. For the inauguration or for the March, we hope you've already booked your lodging, since the prices for everything from the Holiday Inn to a stranger's couch are beyond exorbitant at this point. On a normal weekend, however, we love the infamous Watergate Hotel, of which the Nixonian scandal received its moniker. The hotel closed in 2007, but just re-opened last summer after a $125 million renovation. The revamp includes charming details, like employee uniforms by Mad Men costume designer Jamie Bryant and pens labeled "Stolen from the Watergate Hotel." All of this makes for retro-yet-luxurious vibes that set the perfect stage for enjoying a midday cocktail without judgment.
Our top pick for dining in D.C. Is Bad Saint, which Bon Appetit named the second-best restaurant in America in 2016. ( The New York Times seconded the recommendation just two months ago.) The Filipino restaurant doesn't take reservations, so wait times can be long—here are some tips for getting in.
Other options include: Rasika, known as one of the best Indian restaurants in the country; Rose's Luxury, also a Bon Appetit best-restaurant winner; Blue Duck Tavern, where POTUS and FLOTUS celebrated their anniversary in 2009; Hazel or Maketto for dim sum brunch; Fiola Mare, home to President Obama's 55th birthday celebration; The Red Hen for D.C.'s best Italian; Little Serow, for an affordable prix fixe menu of super-spicy Thai; and Daikaya, for a taste of D.C.'s robust ramen scene.
Tours of the Capitol are free (you can book them here), and we highly recommend you squeeze one in if this is your first time in D.C. The Smithsonian museums are great, and also free (check out the National Museum of the American Indian, it's a favorite), but we definitely suggest prioritizing a visit to the Phillips Collection instead if you're short on time. For something a little less educational, try the 9:30 Club, an iconic music venue where surprise performers often include mega-stars like Radiohead. You should also check out the programming at The Kennedy Center while you're in town, as the building itself is something to behold. And no trip to D.C. Is complete without some time spent at the National Mall, a two-mile stretch of greenery that's also home to some of the nation's most prominent monuments.
To give your wardrobe a D.C.-enabled makeover, make sure to hit up these independent shops: Violet in Georgetown for affordable and on-trend clothes and accessories; Secondi in Dupont for second-hand designer workwear; Redeem for hard-to-find lines like GHSTS and Kowtow; Lynn Louisa for Rachel Comey, Line and other faves; Meeps/Treasury in Adams Morgan for vintage finds; and Relish, for classically tailored pieces.
For home goods, don't miss Miss Pixie's and Salt & Sundry on 14th Street; Salt & Sundry's new sister shop, Little Leaf; and The Eastern Market flea on Saturdays and Sundays, near Capitol Hill.
Book lovers should check out Politics & Prose, which also offers some amazing author events, as well as Capitol Hill Books and Kramerbooks.

According to The Fashion Girl’s Guide to Washington, D.C., some must-visit destinations include The Watergate Hotel for a retro-yet-luxurious stay, Bad Saint for Filipino cuisine, and the Phillips Collection for a unique museum experience. For shopping, check out Violet in Georgetown, Secondi in Dupont for second-hand designer workwear, and Miss Pixie's for home goods. Visitors should also make time for tours of the Capitol and a stroll through the National Mall.

It was a cold winter morning when I walked into the hospital room to see my grandmother for the last time. The sterile smell of the hospital mixed with the blindingly white light of the room was disorienting. A cacophony of beeps and whirs from various machines filled the silence, and somewhere in the distance, a nurse was calling out the rounds.

My grandmother lay on the bed, her eyes closed, and her breaths shallow. Her once plump cheeks were now sunken, and the faint pink color of her skin was fading away. For a moment, it felt like everything was moving in slow motion, and I could feel the weight of my sadness pressing down on my chest.

As I stood there, watching her slowly slipping away, I couldn't help but reflect on the life she had lived. She was a remarkable woman who had experienced moments of both great joy and deep sorrow in her long life. She had taught me so much about life and had always been the one person who believed in me when no one else did.

But as much as I loved her, my memories of her were tinged with regret, for I had taken her for granted. I had always assumed she would be there, loving me, guiding me, and supporting me. I never realized that one day she would be gone, and that realization felt like a punch to my gut.

As I stood there in that sterile room, I realized that life was fleeting, and the people who we love can be taken away from us in the blink of an eye. I promised myself that I would never take anyone for granted again and that I would make it my mission to live a life that would make my grandmother proud.

That day, as I left the hospital, tears streaming down my face, I knew that my life would never be the same. I had been confronted with my own mortality, and it left me with a newfound sense of purpose. I returned to school with a renewed zeal for life, poured my heart into my studies, and made an effort to spend time with the people who mattered to me.

In the years since that day, I have grown and changed in ways that I never thought were possible. I have pursued my dreams, made new friends, and traveled to exciting places. But, most importantly, I have learned to appreciate those around me, to cherish every single moment, and to live life to the fullest. And for that, I will always be thankful for my grandmother and the beautiful life she lived.

Jack had always been a man of science. After all, it was the pursuit of knowledge and the laws of the universe that had kept him engrossed in his work as a laboratory assistant for several years. It was a routine job with little glamor, but he loved the thrill of discovery and the challenge of taking something unknown and working with it until its secrets were laid bare.

One fateful morning, he was working in the lab when he accidentally spilled a container of experimental chemicals on himself. It wasn't until later that day, while he was relaxing in his living room, that he realized something had irrevocably changed within him.

Jack had been dumbfounded, to say the least, but as he experimented with his newfound ability, he swiftly realized that he could control the element of fire with a mere thought.

As his powers grew in strength and finesse over the following days, Jack began to feel a sense of euphoria that he had never experienced before. But with that exhilaration came a creeping sense of unease, a nagging doubt within him that his powers might not be entirely his to wield. As he struggled to come to grips with his abilities, Jack found himself pursued by a shadowy figure who wanted nothing more than possession of his power. This person was a scientist, like Jack himself, but unlike Jack, this man saw the power of fire as a tool of destruction, something to be used for striking against those that he deemed enemies.

Jack was determined to use his power for good, and the good of all, and he knew he could only do that by giving up his quest for knowledge.

It was a hard decision, but it was one that he knew he had to make. And as the years went by, Jack contented himself with a quiet, ordinary life. He had given up his pursuit of knowledge, but he had gained something far more significant in exchange - peace. The power within him had faded away, and the world had forgotten about him, but Jack remained a man of science, a man of the universe. And that was all that mattered in the end.

This is a simple recipe for enchiladas that I have made several times. It’s quick and easy. I sometimes make it ahead of time and refrigerate for a few hours before baking.
Brown the ground beef and drain the fat off.
Add the can of Rotel and let the beef and Rotel simmer until the juice is gone.
Bake at 350º for approximately 30 minutes – until bubbly and golden.
To make it even easier stack the enchiladas instead of rolling them. Put a little sauce on the bottom of an 8 or 9” cake pan or other baking dish. Moisten a tortilla with some sauce and top it with filling and a little cheese. Repeat, stacking tortillas and filling on top of each other. I use a total of 5 tortillas in a stack. Don’t put filling on the 5th tortilla. Pour some sauce over the last tortilla and top the stack with cheese. 5 tortillas works for me because the stack doesn’t get so high that starts sliding over, and tortillas typically come in packages that are multiples of 10. Bake just like you would rolled enchiladas.

- If you're feeling adventurous, try making your own enchilada sauce from scratch using chili powder, cumin, tomato sauce, and chicken broth.

Which artists were part of the Renaissance movement and how did their work transform European art and culture?

Some of the prominent artists of the Renaissance movement include Leonardo da Vinci, Michelangelo, Raphael, Sandro Botticelli, Titian, Jan van Eyck, Albrecht Dürer, and Donatello.

Their work transformed European art and culture in various ways. They shifted the focus from religious themes to a more secular, humanistic approach. They emphasized the importance of individualism, realism, and scientific observation in art. They rediscovered the classical styles of Greece and Rome and brought them into their own work, leading to a revival of interest in antiquity. Their use of linear perspective and chiaroscuro techniques created a more realistic depiction of space and depth, adding a new level of sophistication to European art. Overall, the Renaissance artists' work challenged the traditional ways of creating and interpreting art, paving the way for future artistic movements and changing the cultural landscape of Europe.

What were some of the key historical events that occurred during the 3rd century AD that had a lasting impact on Western civilization?

1. Crisis of the Third Century: A period of political instability and economic decline in the Roman Empire, marked by frequent changes in rulers, civil wars, invasions by barbarian tribes, and inflation.

2. Rise of Christianity: Christianity emerged as a major religion during the 3rd century, and its spread had a profound impact on Western civilization.

3. Diocletian's Reforms: Emperor Diocletian implemented a series of reforms to strengthen the Roman Empire, including the division of the empire into two administrative regions, the creation of a new system of tax collection, and the establishment of a standing army.

4. Construction of Roman Infrastructure: Many important structures and buildings were built during this time, including the Colosseum and the expansion of the Roman road network.

5. Battle of Adrianople: In 378 AD, the Roman army suffered a devastating defeat at the hands of the Goths, leading to the death of Emperor Valens and the weakening of the Eastern Roman Empire.

6. Growth of Gothic Kingdoms: In the aftermath of the Battle of Adrianople, Gothic tribes established their own kingdoms in Europe, including the Visigothic Kingdom in Spain and the Ostrogothic Kingdom in Italy.

7. Spread of Greek Learning: Greek literature, philosophy, and art continued to thrive and spread during the 3rd century, laying the foundation for the Renaissance several centuries later.

Provide a comprehensive explanation of the contrasts and disparities between client-side and server-side rendering in web development, taking into account the advantages and disadvantages of each rendering approach in terms of performance, user experience, search engine optimization, scalability, security, and compatibility with various devices and browsers. Include relevant examples and use cases to illustrate your points. Additionally, discuss the relationship between the rendering method and the architecture of the web application, and recommend the ideal rendering technique for different scenarios based on their requirements and goals.

Client-side and server-side rendering are two approaches used in web development to render web pages to end-users. Client-side rendering involves using JavaScript to render web pages on the client-side, while server-side rendering involves rendering web pages on the server-side before sending the pre-rendered HTML page to the end-user. Each approach has its own advantages and disadvantages, and the choice of which approach to use depends on a variety of factors.

Performance:

In terms of performance, client-side rendering is usually faster because the HTML page is already loaded, and the application only needs to fetch the data and render it. On the other hand, server-side rendering involves rendering the entire HTML page on the server before sending it to the client, which often takes more time. However, client-side rendering can lead to slow initial page load times, especially for large applications, whereas server-side rendering can lead to faster initial page loads.

User Experience:

In terms of user experience, client-side rendering provides a more interactive experience because the application can easily update and change parts of the page without reloading the entire page, which can make the application feel more responsive. On the other hand, server-side rendering may result in a less interactive experience as the page reloads every time the user interacts with the application.

Search Engine Optimization:

In terms of search engine optimization, server-side rendering is often preferred because it provides better SEO. Search engines prefer to crawl and index pages that are already rendered on the server, which is why server-side rendering is often preferred for SEO purposes. On the other hand, client-side rendering can make it difficult for search engines to evaluate the content of the page.

Scalability:

In terms of scalability, client-side rendering is more scalable than server-side rendering because the processing is done on the client-side, which reduces the load on the server. This makes it easier to scale an application as the number of users increases. On the other hand, server-side rendering can be more difficult to scale because the server needs to render and process each page request.

Security:

In terms of security, server-side rendering is generally more secure than client-side rendering because the server is responsible for rendering and providing the HTML page to the client, which can help prevent malicious attacks. On the other hand, client-side rendering can expose the application to potential security threats.

Compatibility with Devices and Browsers:

In terms of compatibility with different devices and browsers, server-side rendering is generally more compatible because it only requires a web browser to display the page correctly. On the other hand, client-side rendering requires the user's device to have JavaScript enabled, which can limit the compatibility of the application.

Relationship between Rendering Method and Application Architecture:

The choice of rendering method is closely related to the application architecture. For example, if an application requires a lot of interactivity and real-time updates, client-side rendering may be the ideal choice. However, if an application requires strong SEO and content visibility, server-side rendering is the optimal choice. Additionally, the server-side rendering is generally preferred when applications need to handle large amounts of data or require faster load times.

Ideal Rendering Technique for Different Scenarios:

Based on their requirements and goals, different scenarios require different rendering techniques. For example, if the goal is to create an interactive single-page application with real-time updates, client-side rendering may be preferred. However, if the goal is to optimize SEO and ensure content visibility, server-side rendering may be the ideal choice. Additionally, for applications that require quick initial loading times, server-side rendering is the better option. 

In conclusion, the choice of rendering technique in web development depends on the requirements and goals of the application. Both client-side and server-side rendering methods offer different benefits and drawbacks in terms of performance, user experience, SEO, scalability, security and compatibility with different devices and browsers. To determine which rendering method is optimal, developers need to carefully analyze the application's purpose and requirements, and make an informed decision based on those factors.

FADE IN:

EXT. VINEYARD - DAY

CUT TO:

JIM

(smiling)

Read the passage below and answer the question or follow the instruction: What is your opinion of the remastered version of the film, and how does it compare to the original quality?

Passage: 'The Man From Earth' gets the Special Edition treatment. A strong story, lots of extras, but the remastered look isn't great.
Ten years ago, The Man From Earth was released to the world. Not in theatres; the low-budget, indie film went straight to DVD. But with an excellent cast and cred for the writer, the movie went on to critical acclaim. It scored nominations, awards, and topped the list of Best Films in its genre. It was also, unfortunately, heavily pirated. Now, with an impending sequel, the original gets a remastered Special Edition release.
The story is a great thought experiment. Professor John Oldman (David Lee Smith, CSI: Miami) is packing up to leave town unexpectedly. A group of his colleagues insist on having a going-away party. When he slips out, they follow him and demand an explanation for his attempted disappearance. John tells them he’s actually a 14,000-year-old caveman who moves along every ten years before people notice that he doesn’t age. Of course, no one believes him. But the more they try to poke holes in his story, while he can’t prove what he’s saying is true, they fail to disprove it, either.
The Man From Earth plays very much like a play. Almost all the action is on one set, taking place in a single day. The ensemble by and large all stay on camera for the duration, making it a dialogue-heavy conversation piece. There isn’t any action, per se, just an intense examination of the claim and the ramifications of such a thing, exploring both the practical and the historical. Given that the characters are college professors, the conversation is high-brow and intelligent, covering a wide variety of angles.
The ensemble cast also has plenty of Star Trek cred in it. Among them are John Billingsley (a lead in Star Trek: Enterprise), Tony Todd (guest star in Star Trek: The Next Generation, Star Trek: Deep Space 9, and Star Trek: Voyager), and Richard Riehle (guest star in Star Trek: The Next Generation, Star Trek: Voyager, and Star Trek: Enterprise). Rounding out the cast are Ellen Crawford (ER), Annika Peterson (Tanner Hall), Alexis Thorpe (Days of Our Lives), and William Katt (Carrie). While not a highly recognizable troupe, these are all working actors who do a good job.
The Man From Earth holds up very well as a story. The plot is engrossing, the actors are natural, and there are enough surprises to make it worth it to pay attention. While it doesn’t answer every question that could be posed, it covers a lot of ground, and Bixby did a great job trying to anticipate what viewers would ask. I’m glad it’s getting a re-release to bring more attention to it.
But despite the expense spent on upgrading the film to HD (which it was not filmed in), I’m not sure the job was good enough to justify it. Sure, the original quality is soft and a bit blurry, but the new version is harsh and grainy. Watching the side-by-side comparison in the Blu-ray special features, I personally appreciated the original better. I’m not saying The Man From Earth couldn’t be made to look higher-quality, but I don’t think this release does it.
There are a wealth of bonus features on the Blu-ray. We get trailers for both the original movie and the upcoming sequel. There are two audio commentaries to choose from. There’s a very entertaining, very short film called “Contagion.” A few featurettes are interesting.
I am loathe to complain about a behind-the-scenes feature, as most are too short for my taste, but the one here is actually too long. Perhaps it would be better split into chunks, as it runs roughly the same length as the film. But I’m not sure that would help much, as there are a lot of unnecessary conversation in it. It’s cool to hear most of the cast, Bixby’s son, a producer, and director Richard Schenkman talk about the unique filming process and the piracy issues. However, there’s repetition and tangents that make it drag on. So for once, I have to say this one could use some editing down.
This is a great film, and I’m very glad to get to see it. It feels indie and low-budget, but that might be a plus for this particular story. The extras, despite my minor complaint that the main one could use some editing down, are plenty and mostly enjoyable. I recommend Jerome Bixby’s The Man From Earth, available now.

What is The Man From Earth about?
The Man From Earth is a thought experiment story about a 14,000-year-old caveman named Professor John Oldman who moves along every ten years before people notice that he doesn’t age. The story follows a group of his colleagues who demand an explanation for his attempted disappearance when he is packing up to leave town unexpectedly. John tells them his story, but no one believes him, and the plot is an intense examination of the claim and the ramifications of such a thing.

In what ways has McDonald's adapted to changing consumer demands for healthier food options?

4. Nutritional information: McDonald's publishes nutritional information about its menu items, helping consumers make informed choices about their food.

How do the concepts of purity and pollution relate to Shinto practices involving shrines and offerings?

The concepts of purity and pollution are essential in Shinto practices involving shrines and offerings. In Shinto, rituals are performed to maintain purity and prevent pollution, which is believed to bring bad luck and disease.

Before entering a shrine, people often cleanse themselves physically to achieve purity. They remove their shoes and wash their hands and mouth using water provided at the shrine.

Furthermore, strict rules of purity govern the preparation of offerings. Food and drink for the kami must be pure and free from impurities. For example, meat, blood, and eggs are considered impure and are not permitted during offerings. Most offerings consist of rice, sake (rice wine), and fruits or vegetables.

In Shintoism, everything in nature has a spirit or kami, and all actions affect the balance between purity and pollution. Therefore, it's essential to maintain purity in all aspects of life to ensure good fortune and protection from impurity.

Simply put, a cannon is a hollow tube containing gunpowder and a projectile inside the tube and a hole or fuse where the user can get fire to the gunpowder and set off an explosion. Gases from the lit gunpowder force the projectile through the tube and into the air.
But how did the Ancient Chinese come up with the idea to create cannons? Well, first they developed gunpowder, which when lit, causes an explosion. Searching for a way to make their emperor live forever, Daoist scholars found that a combination of potassium nitrate, sulfur, and charcoal would explode when lit. This is why gunpowder in Chinese means fire medicine or huǒ yào.
Gunpowder went from its use as a Daoist medicine to a military weapon in the early 900’s during the Tang (618 – 907 CE) dynasty when armies filled hollow bamboo tubes with gunpowder. These first gunpowder-filled tubes were attached to a spear and then thrown at the enemy. This weapon was known as a fire lance.
The soldiers had to be close to the enemy for an accurate hit. The gunpowder would explode, which would result in burns, and other wounds would be suffered from the spear and shards of bamboo from the hollow bamboo tube.
During the Northern Song (960 – 1126 CE), Southern Song (1127 – 1279 CE), and Yuan (1279 – 1368 CE) dynasties, the armies began adding small objects, such as stones, pieces of pottery or metal to the gunpowder-filled fire lance. When the gunpowder was lit, the exploding gas would project the small objects onto the enemy soldiers. No spear was needed as the Ancient Chinese had now invented a gun or a bombard. Crude but effective, these early weapons were the beginning of modern cannons.
Additional early weapons were: gunpowder-filled bombs made from pottery or metal; catapults or trebuchets from which stones were flung or held gunpowder-filled tubes, which when lit exploded projectiles over the enemy; and eruptors holding about one hundred lead balls, which were placed into a chamber on the side of the tube and were moved into the lit gunpowder when the tube was rotated causing the balls to spray out rapidly.
Early Chinese cannons were small guns or bombards, which were made from bronze (a mixture of copper, tin, and minerals such as phosphorus and magnesium). These small weapons were about 14 inches (34 centimeters) long, had an inner diameter (muzzle bore) of 1 inch (2.5 centimeters) and weighed about 8 pounds (3.5 kilograms). They were handheld or placed on a wheeled cart.
In the Yuan dynasty, the bombards remained about the same length, but the inner diameter was bigger (approximately 4 inches or 10 centimeters) and the weight was about twice as much (15 pounds or 7 kilograms) as the earlier style bombard. As the bombards became bigger, the term cannon took over.
Early Chinese cannons were vase shaped – rounded bottoms with a long narrow neck, which provided for a thicker wall of iron around the gunpowder in the bottom of the cannon.
After the Ancient Chinese had a better understanding of how to smelt iron in the late Yuan dynasty, the cannon shaped changed to a long tube and sometimes, the iron was shaped into rings or bands around the longer iron tube shape. The iron rings may have been molded onto the cannon tube to support metal spikes that were used to anchor the cannon to the ground during firing of the gunpowder. These early Chinese cannons were over 2 feet (60 centimeters) long and weighed about 48 pounds (about 22 kilograms).
Prior to the 1500’s during the Ming dynasty, Chinese cannons did not have sights. The cannons were aimed at the enemy with the hope that the projectile would hit its target.
Cannon balls were filled with gunpowder so that when they struck an object, the resulting explosion would cause more harm. They were also filled with chemicals that were poisonous (arsenic), created smoke, burns or blindness (ammonia).
The Ancient Chinese developed repeating or rapid-fire cannons. For example, two cannons were placed on a movable table or cart. After the first cannon was fired at the enemy, the table or cart was moved around into position and the second cannon fired.
Other rapid-fire cannon included a seven-barreled cannon attached to a cart, which had a large central cannon surrounded by six smaller cannon and nine cannons stacked on a stand and lit by one fuse, which fired stone cannon balls weighing 26.5 pounds each (12 kilograms).
Although Chinese cannons were placed on ships during the Yuan dynasty, they really took off as a military weapon during the Ming (1368 – 1644 CE) dynasty. Ancient Chinese generals fighting against the Vietnamese in southern China and the Mongols and tribes in northern China, requested cannons to be used.
Additionally, Chinese cannons were sold or given to South Korea and Japan during the Ming dynasty.
*Chinese hand cannon photo taken by Yannick Trottier. Based on the passage above, Summarize how the Ancient Chinese created cannons and the development of early weapons.

The Ancient Chinese first developed gunpowder and used it in the Tang dynasty to create the fire lance, a spear with a bamboo tube filled with gunpowder. In later dynasties, they added small objects such as stones and pottery to create crude guns or bombards. These early cannons were made of bronze and were handheld or placed on a cart. Over time, they became longer and larger, and iron was used to create rings and bands to support the cannon. Cannonballs were filled with gunpowder and poisonous chemicals. The Ancient Chinese also developed repeating or rapid-fire cannons, which were used by Ming dynasty generals in battles against the Vietnamese, Mongols, and other tribes. Chinese cannons were eventually sold or given to other countries, including South Korea and Japan.

How does the major histocompatibility complex (MHC) contribute to the rejection of grafts in genetically dissimilar individuals?
Generate according to: Trowsdale, John Human Immunogenetics Laboratory, Imperial Cancer Research Fund, London, United Kingdom.
A term used to describe the genes that influence acceptance or rejection of grafts. When grafts of tissue are exchanged between genetically dissimilar individuals, profound immunological rejection generally takes place. In contrast, grafts between genetically similar individuals, such as identical twins, are normally tolerated; they are histocompatible. Most known examples of histocompatibility (or H) genes encode polymorphic (that is, tending to differ between individuals) cell-surface proteins. The major histocompatibility complex (MHC) contains a set of histocompatibility genes, termed major because mismatching at these genes invokes rapid rejection. Other, minor antigens are revealed after precise matching of the major antigens.

The MHC plays a crucial role in activating the immune system to recognize and attack foreign tissue. When a graft from a genetically dissimilar individual is transplanted, its MHC molecules will differ from those on the recipient's own cells. The recipient's immune system will recognize these foreign MHC molecules as non-self and will launch an attack on the transplanted tissue.

In particular, T cells of the immune system recognize foreign MHC molecules through their T cell receptors (TCRs). This recognition triggers a cascade of immune responses including the release of cytokines, activation of killer T cells, and production of antibodies. These responses ultimately lead to the destruction of the transplanted tissue.

Even a single mismatch at a major histocompatibility gene can be enough to trigger rejection. In fact, the MHC is often referred to as the "barrier to transplantation," as it represents the major obstacle to successful transplantation between genetically dissimilar individuals.

Overall, the MHC plays a critical role in determining the compatibility of transplanted tissue and contributes significantly to the rejection of grafts in genetically dissimilar individuals.

H DFTACTGRP(*NO) ACTGRP(*CALLER)

D ARRAY_SIZE      S             10I 0
D ARRAY           S           50A  INZ(*ALL' ')

D MSG             S            9A   INZ(*ALL' ')
D VALID_INPUT     S             1A   INZ(*OFF)
D INPUT_VALUE     S             9A   INZ(*ALL' ')
D SQUARE          S             9P 2 INZ(0)
D MAX_VALUE       S             9I 0 INZ(0)
D MIN_VALUE       S             9I 0 INZ(0)

*------------------------------------------------------------------
* MAIN PROGRAM LOGIC
*------------------------------------------------------------------
C     CALL 'QCMDEXC'                   'CLRSCN'

C     EVAL      MSG = 'ENTER THE SIZE OF ARRAY: '

C                 EVAL      *INLR = *ON
C                 RETURN
C     ENDIF
C                 
C     FOR       I = 1 to ARRAY_SIZE

C                   EVAL      MSG = 'ENTER ELEMENT ' + %CHAR(I) + ': '
C                   CALL      'QSNPRINTF'            INPUT_VALUE 20 '999999999' MSG 
C                   CALL      'CVTCH'                SQUARE    INPUT_VALUE
C                   IF        %ERROR

C                             CALL      'QCMDEXC'   MSG

C                   ENDIF

C                 ENDDO
C     ENDFOR
C                 
C     EVAL      MSG = 'ORIGINAL ARRAY: '
C     CALL      'QCMDEXC'  MSG
C     FOR       I = 1 to ARRAY_SIZE
C                 EVAL      MSG = %CHAR(I) + ': ' + ARRAY(I)
C                 CALL      'QCMDEXC'  MSG
C     ENDFOR
C                 
C     EVAL      MSG = 'SQUARED ARRAY: '
C     CALL      'QCMDEXC'  MSG

C                 ENDIF

*------------------------------------------------------------------

*==================================================================
* END OF PROGRAM 
*==================================================================

7. Send the request: Click on the "Send" button to send the request to the API.

Recently branded as Synergy Law Enforcement Solutions, founder Jason Brennan juggles a full-time job as a sergeant in the Medway Police Department with his work in critical incident planning.
"It's a lot of work, but it's one of those things ... It's one of my passions," he said.
Brennan started the company in 2001 with his friend, Franklin Police Detective Chris Baker. The two started working as consultants for local police departments and later expanded to serve private companies and schools. They work out of an office in Franklin.

Here is a piece of text: A recent survey indicates that health care has made little progress toward value-based care (VBC) since last year, with more than two-thirds (67 percent) of physicians and health plan executives indicating that U.S. Health care is still predominantly a fee-for-service system.
The findings come at the same time that the Center for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) has announced a slew of proposals that have, among other things, reduced the amount of total incentives available for redistribution to eligible physicians who meet quality thresholds under the Merit-Based Incentive Systems Program (MIPS) for Medicare beneficiaries.
According to Dr. L Patrick James, Chief Clinical Officer of Quest Diagnostics, who conducted the survey, a majority of physicians believe they do not have the tools or the data to succeed in a value-based contracting environment.
The slowdown in the shift towards value-based care has several ramifications.
Many of the components of value-based care, namely data and analytics, remote monitoring, enhanced patient engagement and improved caregiver communications are all part of the ongoing digital transformation of health care. Investing in these programs continues to make economic sense only when there is money to be made doing so, and cease to have any meaning when the system of incentives diminishes the monetary benefits of these programs.
With the stalling of the shift to value-based care, health systems are likely feeling the impact of margin compression as reimbursements under the traditional fee-for-service model continue to fall. Discretionary dollars are more likely to go towards maintaining and upgrading essential infrastructure, and in optimizing existing IT investments. The appetite for big-ticket technology investments, especially for digital initiatives, is likely to be low, except for targeted investments with clearly identifiable returns on investment.
It’s safe to say that the debate on health care’s future in data has been put to rest. However, as indicated by the Quest survey, it appears that physicians are overwhelmed by the flood of data, and making the data actionable is a crucial challenge today. Poor data, along with a lack of adequate tools, impact the ability of physicians to qualify for incentives under the MIPS scheme, forcing them to stay with fee-for-service payment models even in an era of declining reimbursements.
Across industries, there is more downbeat news on digital transformation. A recent study by consulting firm Capgemini and the MIT Center for Digital Business concludes that organizations are struggling to convert their digital investments into business successes. The reasons are illuminating and many: lack of digital leadership skills, and a lack of alignment between IT and business, to name a couple. The study goes on to suggest that companies have underestimated the challenge of digital transformation and that organizations have done a poor job of engaging employees across the enterprise in the digital transformation journey.
These findings may sound surprising to technology vendors, all of whom have gone “digital” in anticipation of big rewards from the digital bonanza (at least one global consulting firm has gone so far as to tie senior executive compensation to “digital” revenues). Anecdotally, “digital” revenues are still under 30 percent of total revenues for most technology firms, which further corroborates the findings of market studies on the state of digital transformation.
Despite the somber survey findings, health systems continue to invest in initiatives that deliver tangible, near-term benefits. An example of a high priority investment area is patient access. At Providence St Joseph Medical system, a focus on online scheduling has delivered savings of $3 to 4 per appointment booked, producing over $300,000 in total savings to the health system. As a bonus, there are fewer no-shows when patients book online, which results in additional bottom-line benefits to the hospital. Since labor is around 60 percent of a hospital’s costs, any digital solution that has a labor substitution component and increases productivity is a target for health system executives. The rising popularity of voice-enablement in caregiver communications is a case in point.
Which leads me to the title of this blog: is digital a game of small numbers? The point solutions referred to above seem to suggest that to be the case, at least as it relates to digital. Health care is no stranger to big numbers, considering the many millions each hospital has invested in implementing electronic health record (EHR) systems over the last decade. However, it seems unlikely that we will see such investment levels in digital, at least in the short term. Part of the reason is that there no single, monolithic digital platform that can perform the tasks at the scale and scope of a foundational transaction system like EHR. The digital health solution provider market is highly fragmented, and there is a shortage of ready-to-deploy “last mile solutions” which I have discussed in an earlier column here.

Can you provide a recipe for both Thai curry and Indian curry?

Yes, here are two recipes for Thai curry and Indian curry:

Thai Green Curry:

Ingredients: 

1 tbsp oil 
1 onion, diced 
2 garlic cloves, crushed 
2 tbsp green curry paste 
400ml can coconut milk 
1 red pepper, sliced 
1 green pepper, sliced 
1 courgette, sliced 
250g cherry tomatoes 
400g tofu, cut into cubes 
3 tbsp soy sauce 
1 tbsp brown sugar 
juice of 1 lime 
basil leaves, to garnish 

Instructions: 

1. Heat the oil in a large saucepan and add the onion and garlic. Fry for 2-3 minutes, until softened. 

2. Add the green curry paste and stir well. Cook for 2-3 minutes, until fragrant. 

3. Pour in the can of coconut milk and stir well. Add the peppers, courgette, and cherry tomatoes. 

4. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally. 

5. Add the tofu cubes, soy sauce, and brown sugar. Bring back to a simmer for another 5 minutes. 

6. Add the lime juice and stir well. Serve hot, garnished with basil leaves. 

Indian Chicken Curry:

Ingredients: 

2 tbsp vegetable oil 
1 onion, finely diced 
2 cloves garlic, crushed 
1 tsp grated ginger 
1 tbsp curry powder 
1 tsp ground turmeric 
1 tsp ground cumin 
1 tsp ground coriander 
1/2 tsp paprika 
1/2 tsp salt 
1/2 tsp black pepper 
500g chicken breast, cut into bite-sized pieces 
400ml can coconut milk 
1 tbsp tomato paste 
1 green bell pepper, diced 
1 red bell pepper, diced 
fresh cilantro, for garnish 

Instructions: 

1. Heat the vegetable oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add the onion, garlic, and ginger. Cook for 2-3 minutes, until softened. 

2. Add the curry powder, turmeric, cumin, coriander, paprika, salt, and black pepper. Cook for another minute until fragrant. 

3. Add the chicken pieces and stir to coat with the spice mixture. Cook for 3-4 minutes until browned. 

4. Pour in the coconut milk and stir well. Add the tomato paste and stir again. 

5. Add the diced green and red bell peppers. Stir well and reduce the heat to low. 

6. Cover the saucepan and let simmer for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the chicken is cooked through and the bell peppers are tender. 

7. Garnish with fresh cilantro and serve hot with rice or naan bread.

Write a comprehensive report on the positive and negative impact of automation on customer service in the business industry. Use relevant data, case studies, and examples to support your arguments. Draw from reputable sources and adopt a clear, logical structure while maintaining a formal writing style. Ensure your report provides insights on how businesses can strike a balance using automation to improve customer service without compromising personalization and human interaction in service delivery. The report should not exceed 3000 words.

Introduction

Automation has become a buzzword in recent times, with businesses increasingly moving towards automation for many of their operations. In the customer service industry, automation has become an essential tool in improving efficiency, reducing costs, and increasing customer satisfaction. Automation refers to the use of technology to automate many of the processes and services that were previously done manually. The technology was mainly used in industries that required a high degree of accuracy and speed, such as manufacturing. However, it has gradually spread to other sectors, including customer service. This report aims to explore the positive and negative impacts of automation on customer service in the business industry. 

Positive Impacts of Automation on Customer Service 

1. Increased Efficiency

One of the most significant benefits of automation in customer service is increased efficiency. Many businesses have automated their customer service processes, such as responding to incoming calls or emails, collecting customer feedback, and resolving issues. Automation reduces the time and resources required to perform these tasks, enabling businesses to handle a more significant volume of customer queries and complaints with fewer staff. For example, chatbots have become a popular form of customer service automation in recent years, with many businesses using them to handle simple customer inquiries promptly. 

2. 24/7 Availability

Another advantage of automation in customer service is the ability to operate on a 24/7 schedule. Automated chatbots or email reply systems can work around the clock, providing customers with around-the-clock support. This is essential for businesses that operate in different time zones or have a global customer base. 

3. Cost Savings

Automation in customer service can also lead to significant cost savings for businesses. By reducing the need for extensive customer service teams, businesses can cut down on staffing costs. Automation also ensures that customers receive prompt responses to their inquiries, reducing the need for additional follow-up services. 

4. Improved Data Management

Automation in customer service also helps businesses collect and manage data more efficiently. Customer information, feedback, and concerns can be collected, analyzed, and stored in a centralized system, enabling businesses to track trends and make data-driven decisions. This helps businesses identify areas that require improvement and tailor their customer service strategies to meet customer needs better. 

Negative Impacts of Automation on Customer Service 

1. Reduced Personalization 

One of the primary drawbacks of automation in customer service is the potential for reduced personalization. Automated processes such as chatbots or auto-reply systems are designed to provide standard responses to common customer inquiries. However, they may not be able to provide personalized service or understand the unique needs and preferences of individual customers. This can lead to a lack of empathy and customer dissatisfaction. 

2. Negative Perception Among Customers 

Automation can also create a negative perception among customers. Many customers prefer human interaction over automated systems, and the use of chatbots or self-service portals may make customers feel undervalued or unimportant. This can lead to a decline in customer satisfaction and loyalty, affecting a business's bottom line. 

3. Technical Glitches

Another downside of automation in customer service is the potential for technical glitches. Technology can sometimes fail, leading to delayed responses, incorrect information, or no response at all. This can lead to frustration among customers and a decline in trust and confidence in the business. 

4. Overreliance on Automation 

Lastly, overreliance on automation can pose a risk to businesses. Automated processes may become too ingrained in a business's operations, and a single technical glitch or failure could lead to a significant breakdown in service delivery. Businesses need to have backup systems in place to ensure continuity of service in the event of a technological failure. 

Striking a Balance

Businesses can strike a balance using automation to improve customer service without compromising personalization and human interaction in service delivery. 

1. Invest in Hybrid Systems

Investing in hybrid systems that use both automation and human staff can help businesses provide personalized, efficient, and reliable customer service. For example, businesses can implement self-service portals or chatbots for simple inquiries, with the option of reaching out to human staff for more complex queries. 

2. Ensure Proper Training for Staff

Businesses must also ensure that human staff are trained to use automation systems efficiently. This includes training staff on how to use chatbots, auto-reply systems, and other automation tools to ensure that they are providing prompt and accurate responses to customers. 

3. Regularly Test Systems 

Regular testing of automation systems can help businesses identify potential glitches and areas of improvement. This can help businesses create backup plans to ensure business continuity in the event of a system failure. 

Conclusion 

In conclusion, automation in customer service has both positive and negative impacts on businesses. While automation can increase efficiency, save costs, and provide 24/7 availability, it can also lead to reduced personalization, negative perception among customers, technical glitches, and overreliance on automation. To ensure that businesses strike a balance between automation and personalization, hybrid systems, training for staff, and regular testing of systems are critical. Ultimately, businesses must focus on providing personalized, efficient, and reliable customer service

Write instructions for cleaning a dishwasher filter.

1. First, make sure the dishwasher is completely turned off and unplugged.
2. Locate the dishwasher filter. It is usually located at the bottom of the dishwasher, near the spray arm.
3. Remove the filter by pulling up and out.
4. Rinse the filter under warm water to remove any loose debris and food particles.
5. Use a soft-bristled brush, like an old toothbrush, to gently scrub the filter, paying close attention to any caked-on debris.
6. For extra cleaning power, mix a solution of warm water and dish soap in a bowl and soak the filter for about 10-15 minutes.
7. Rinse the filter thoroughly under warm water to remove all soap and debris.
8. Dry the filter with a clean towel or let it air dry before placing it back in the dishwasher.
9. Once the filter is dry, insert it back into the dishwasher, making sure it snaps securely into place.
10. Finally, plug in and turn on the dishwasher to make sure everything is working properly.

Can you provide a thorough explanation of the importance of version control in the development of software, including the main principles and techniques used? Please include examples of how version control has improved software development processes and reduced errors or conflicts.

Version control is a crucial tool in the development of software, providing developers with an effective way to manage and track changes made to the codebase over time. It allows multiple users to work on the same codebase while ensuring that everyone is using the same version of the code and that changes are properly documented, tracked, and reviewed.

The main principles of version control include the ability to create, manage, and track changes to the software codebase, along with the ability to revert to previous versions of the code if needed. It also allows for collaboration between team members through features such as branching and merging, allowing multiple users to work on different parts of the same codebase without interfering with each other.

Some of the most commonly used version control techniques include centralized version control, distributed version control, and Git. Each technique has its own advantages and disadvantages, with Git being one of the most popular and widely used version control systems due to its speed, flexibility, and reliability.

One of the most significant benefits of version control is that it helps to reduce errors and conflicts that can arise when multiple developers are working on the same codebase. By providing a centralized location for the code, developers can easily review changes made by others, identify potential conflicts, and resolve any issues before they cause further problems.

Version control also provides developers with a complete history of changes made to the codebase, allowing for greater transparency and accountability regarding the development process. This can be particularly useful in large or complex software projects, where multiple developers are involved and changes need to be tracked and managed over an extended period.

Overall, version control is a critical tool for software development, providing developers with a reliable and efficient means of managing code changes, collaborating with team members, and reducing errors and conflicts. Its use has significantly improved software development processes, leading to the creation of higher quality software in a more efficient and effective manner.

What is the history of the Bauhaus school of design and how did it influence modern architecture?

The Bauhaus school of design was a German art school that operated from 1919 to 1933, with the stated goal of uniting art and industry to create a better design. The school was founded by architect Walter Gropius, who sought to forge an interdisciplinary approach to design that would break down the traditional boundaries between art, craft, and technology.

The Bauhaus curriculum emphasized the importance of both theory and practice. Students were trained in design principles and techniques, as well as in the use of modern materials and production methods. The school attracted a diverse array of students and faculty, including artists, architects, designers, and craftsmen from across Europe and beyond.

The design philosophy of the Bauhaus emphasized simplicity, functionality, and utility. The school's famous motto, "form follows function," reflected this emphasis on practicality and efficiency above all else. Bauhaus designs also embraced new technologies and materials, such as steel, glass, and concrete, and rejected ornamentation and excessive decoration.

The influence of the Bauhaus on modern architecture and design was profound. The school's minimalist aesthetic and emphasis on function over form had a lasting impact on the design of buildings, furniture, and other objects. Many of the school's graduates went on to become influential architects and designers in their own right, spreading the ideals of the Bauhaus around the world.

Perhaps most important, however, was the way in which the Bauhaus challenged traditional notions of art and design, advocating for a more holistic approach that emphasized the integration of art into daily life. The school's innovative ideas and experimental approach made it a revolutionary force in the world of design and continue to inspire designers and architects today.

That's part of the fun of coming to the festival, I make it a point to come every year, at least to a couple of showings." This year, the festival, which regularly brings in celebrity guests to talk about the classic films in which they starred, included appearances by actress Louise Fletcher and Cindy Williams. Fletcher won an Academy Award for her portrayal of Nurse Ratched in the 1975 film "One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest." Williams, best known for her role as Shirley Feeney in the hit television show "Laverne & Shirley" in the 1970s and '80s, appeared at a screening of George Lucas' first hit film "American Graffiti" on Friday. "Cindy Williams is a sweetheart," Doug Pullen, the festival's creative director, said. "We had a private reception for her before (her appearance). One of the festival's best attended events was the Aug. 8 free outdoor screening of the campy musical "The Rocky Horror Picture Show," Pullen said. He estimated more than 4,000 film-lovers enjoyed the cult classic whose fans enjoy dressing up as its characters, acting out the film as it plays and various other traditions such as throwing toast and rice at various points in the movie. The 1939 epic Civil War romance "Gone With the Wind" and the 1985 time travel adventure "Back to the Future," were both equally well attended, attracting about 1,600 people each, Pullen said. "I think it's great that we have people interested in seeing films spanning 46 years," Pullen said. Another annual tradition which has kept people coming to the festival year after year is the theater's light show, which illuminates the ceiling in a night sky scene, and the Mighty Wurlitzer Organ, played on the final day by Ken Fedorick and several other volunteers throughout the festival. "I love the theater," West El Pasoan Debbie Hinshaw said. "I love when they show the stars and the organ. Campers were taught filmmaking basics and made short films which were screened, along with other local shorts and features, in the El Paso Community Foundation's Foundation Room, located just around the corner from the Plaza on Oregon Street. The camp had 18 participants and Pullen said it will return for next year's festival. The Local Flavor series, featuring local filmmakers, has also continued to grow, Pullen said. Some of the screenings played to a capacity audience, he said. "Last year we tripled the previous year's attendance (for Local Flavor) and we can safely say we had a higher attendance this year," Pullen said. Part of what makes the festival possible each year is the work of many volunteers who take tickets, usher people to their seats and answer questions for festival-goers. Luis Suira is a second-year volunteer. He decided to volunteer because he liked the festival and the theater it calls home. "I think bringing classic films to El Paso is a great way to bring the community together in a truly fantastic place," Suira said. He's already making mental notes for next year's Plaza Classic, which is set for Aug. 4-14, and the festival's tenth anniversary in two years. While no concrete plans are in place yet, other than the dates, he hopes to continue the Plaza Classic's partnerships with the El Paso Chihuahuas and with the El Paso museums of art and history. The baseball movie "The Natural," starring Robert Redford kicked off the festival two weeks ago at Southwest University Park and the two Downtown museums hosted events and exhibits around the screenings of "Gone With the Wind" and several of pop artist Andy Warhol's films. Write a guide for making a delicious beef Stroganoff.

Beef stroganoff is a rich and creamy dish that originated in Russia. It’s made with tender strips of beef, mushrooms, onion, sour cream, and served over egg noodles. In this recipe, we’ll show you how to make a delicious beef stroganoff in just a few easy steps.

Here’s what you’ll need:

Ingredients:

- 1 lb. Beef sirloin, cut into thin strips
- 1 large onion, chopped
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 cup sliced mushrooms
- 1 tbsp. Tomato paste
- 1 tbsp. Worcestershire sauce
- 1 tsp. Dijon mustard
- 1 tsp. Dried thyme
- 1 1/2 cups beef broth
- 1/2 cup sour cream
- 2 tbsp. Chopped fresh parsley
- Salt and pepper to taste
- 8 oz. Egg noodles

Instructions:

1. Cook noodles according to package instructions in boiling salted water. Drain and set aside.

2. Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add beef and cook until browned on both sides. Remove from the pan and set aside.

3. In the same skillet, add onions and mushrooms and cook until softened.

4. Add garlic, tomato paste, Worcestershire sauce and dried thyme to the pan and stir well.

5. Stir in beef broth until fully incorporated. Bring to a simmer and reduce heat to low. Cover and let cook for 15 minutes.

6. After 15 minutes, check the consistency of the sauce. If it’s too thin or watery, let it simmer for another 5-10 minutes until it thickens.

7. Remove the lid from the skillet and add the sour cream to the pan. Stir well until fully incorporated.

8. Return the beef to the skillet and heat through.

9. Serve the beef stroganoff over the cooked egg noodles and garnish with fresh parsley.

Your beef stroganoff is ready! Enjoy your delicious and creamy meal with your family or friends.

Passage: The collapse of oil prices to levels unseen since the early 2000s has shaken markets and confidence in the health of major economies. Experts include the lifting of economic sanctions on Iran as a key factor in the dramatic fall. Yet, there is no consensus on this point.
In a recent paper, we quantify the global effects of this change in Iran’s trading opportunities, focusing on the countries that are likely to be most affected by the lifting of the oil embargo. The 2012 restrictions imposed by the European Union on Iran were the most far-reaching sanction as they curtailed the sales of Iran’s most important export commodity.
We also capture other components of the nuclear deal: the expected reduction in Iran’s trading costs and the liberalisation of cross-border trade in financial and transport services. The global effects of these two components are small as Iran accounts for a negligible share of the world’s non-oil trade.
Assuming that Iran is able to increase oil production and exports to the EU to pre-embargo levels, we estimate that the oil price will decline by 13 percent (or about $3 a barrel at current prices).
This decline implies losses for the net oil-exporting nations that are steepest for Opec members, especially the Gulf Cooperation Council states, which as a group loses nearly four percent in per capita welfare. The losses are due to the deterioration in their terms of trade.
As many of them subsidise oil, the lower oil price will have a compensating efficiency gain, but not enough to reverse the welfare loss. By contrast, oil-importing economies are expected to benefit – mostly because of improvements in their terms of trade, but also because cheaper oil enables expansion of industries that use crude oil and because in most of these countries oil use is taxed.
In percentage terms, the gains to the oil-importing countries are modest, mostly in the range of between a quarter and half a percent, but the world as a whole is better off as the gains to oil importers outweigh the losses to oil exporters.
As expected, the lifting of the economic sanctions is most beneficial to Iran, where per capita welfare is expected to rise by almost four percent. The gains are due to the expansion of oil production and exports and the liberalisation of cross-border trade in financial and transport services.
Importantly, the magnitude of the estimated oil price change suggests that the dramatic oil price drop observed since 2015 has little to do with the anticipated lifting of Iran’s oil embargo. Other factors have been driving down the price of oil.
Iran’s gains may be much more modest if Iranians are unable to increase oil production or oil exports to their pre-embargo levels. We estimate that a bounce back to just half of Iran’s pre-embargo oil exports to the EU is associated with per capita welfare gains of only three percent (oil prices will correspondingly decline by less).
Iran can get the most benefit from the lifting of sanctions by implementing reforms that improve the competitiveness of its economy.
For example, unilateral reductions of Iranian tariffs on imports of capital goods could add half a percentage point to the gains expected in the baseline scenario, as this reform enhances companies’ ability to upgrade their factories and import new technology.
Reforms in support of the recovery of the domestic car sector could increase per capita welfare in Iran by an additional 1.5 percentage points.

The recent collapse of oil prices is not solely due to the lifting of economic sanctions on Iran; other factors have also been driving down prices. However, Iran's increased oil production and exports could lead to a further decline in oil prices by 13 percent. This would have a negative impact on net oil-exporting nations, particularly OPEC members, while oil-importing countries would benefit. The lifting of sanctions is most beneficial to Iran, where per capita welfare is expected to rise by almost four percent, but this could be further increased through reforms to improve the competitiveness of its economy.

Please outline a recipe for a creamy and flavorful vegan pumpkin soup that is completely free of gluten and dairy. It should include detailed instructions for how to prepare the ingredients, time estimates for each step, and suggestions for any necessary substitutions or variations. Please also provide tips for seasoning and garnishing the soup, as well as recommendations for how to store and reheat any leftovers. Finally, please make sure that the recipe is clear and easy to follow for beginners and novice cooks alike.

Creamy Vegan Pumpkin Soup (Gluten-Free and Dairy-Free)

Ingredients:
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 onion, diced
- 3 garlic cloves, minced
- 1 red bell pepper, diced
- 1 can (15 oz) pumpkin puree
- 2 cups vegetable broth
- 1 can (14 oz) coconut milk
- 1 tsp ground cumin
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 1/4 tsp ground cinnamon
- 1/4 tsp ground nutmeg
- Salt and pepper, to taste
- 1 tbsp maple syrup
- Chopped fresh parsley or cilantro, for garnish

Instructions:

1. Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion and garlic, and sauté for 2-3 minutes, until fragrant.

2. Add the red bell pepper and cook for another 3-4 minutes, until softened.

3. Add the pumpkin puree, vegetable broth, coconut milk, cumin, smoked paprika, cinnamon, nutmeg, salt, and pepper. Stir well to combine.

4. Bring the soup to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally.

5. Using an immersion blender, blend the soup until smooth and creamy. If you don't have an immersion blender, you can transfer the soup to a blender and blend in batches.

6. Stir in the maple syrup and let the soup simmer for another 5 minutes. Taste and adjust seasoning, if necessary.

7. Ladle the soup into bowls and garnish with chopped fresh parsley or cilantro. Serve hot.

Storage and Reheating:

Leftover soup can be stored in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 5 days or in the freezer for up to 2 months.

To reheat the soup, simply warm it up on the stove over medium heat until heated through, stirring occasionally. You may need to add a splash of water or vegetable broth to thin it out if it has thickened in the fridge or freezer. 

Notes:

- If you can't find pumpkin puree, you can use butternut squash puree or sweet potato puree instead.
- You can adjust the spices to your liking. Add more smoked paprika for a smokier flavor or more cinnamon for a sweeter taste.
- For a creamier soup, use full-fat coconut milk. Light coconut milk will result in a thinner soup.
- Consider serving the soup with some gluten-free bread or crackers on the side.

What is the significance of the Tet holiday in Vietnam, and how do families typically celebrate this event?

Tet, also known as the Vietnamese Lunar New Year, is the most significant holiday in Vietnam. It marks the beginning of the lunar calendar and typically falls in late January or early February. The holiday lasts for about a week and is a time for family reunions, feasting, and reflection.

The significance of Tet lies in its role as a time for renewal and starting anew. It is a time to pay respects to one's ancestors and to seek blessings for the coming year. Many families will clean their homes thoroughly before the holiday, decorate them with red banners and flowers, and offer offerings at the family altar.

Tet is also a time for feasting and enjoying special holiday foods. Traditional dishes include banh chung (a sticky rice cake wrapped in banana leaves), mut (candied fruits), and thit kho (braised pork belly).

Another important aspect of Tet is the giving of lucky money (li xi) to children and unmarried adults. This is often done in red envelopes and is believed to bring good luck and prosperity in the coming year.

Overall, Tet is a time of renewal, reflection, and celebration for families in Vietnam. It is a deeply important cultural event that is steeped in tradition and meaning.

Ingredients:
- 1 pound ground beef
- 1/2 cup bread crumbs
- 1 egg
- 1/4 cup minced onion
- 1/4 cup minced bell pepper
- 1/4 cup ketchup
- 1 tablespoon Worcestershire sauce
- Salt and pepper to taste
- Sliced bread
- Mayonnaise
- Mustard
- Lettuce
- Tomato

Instructions:

1. Preheat the oven to 375°F.

2. In a large bowl, combine the ground beef, bread crumbs, egg, minced onion, minced bell pepper, ketchup, Worcestershire sauce, salt, and pepper. Mix well with your hands.

6. When the meatloaf is done, remove it from the oven and let it cool for a few minutes. Use a serrated knife to slice the meatloaf into thick slices.

7. Spread mayonnaise and/or mustard on one side of each slice of bread.

8. Top one slice of bread with a slice of meatloaf, followed by a handful of lettuce and a few slices of tomato. Top with the other slice of bread.

9. Repeat with the remaining bread, meatloaf, lettuce, and tomato slices until all your sandwiches are assembled.

10. Serve your meatloaf sandwiches on a large platter, or pack them up for a picnic or lunch on-the-go.

Write a step-by-step how-to guide for creating a visually appealing flower arrangement using seasonal blooms and foliage. Step-by-step how-to guide for creating a visually appealing flower arrangement using seasonal blooms and foliage:

Materials needed:
- Floral foam or vase
- Pruning shears
- Water
- Selection of seasonal flowers and foliage
- Unique elements (optional)

Step 1: Choose a vase or floral foam that can accommodate your flower arrangement. Make sure it is tall enough to provide support to your flowers, and wide enough for the floral foam or stems to fit in.
